title: QWEEPS visual lesson pipeline as scanned
question: How does a browser request move through the loopback studio, lesson preparation, rendering, review, narration and playback?
representation: Inspect-only static source trace in 3 beats: browser entry, Python preparation, render/review/playback. Groups are file containers with internal operations; edges are scanned import/reference relations, not runtime calls. No packets, no runtime state, no cloud or database; loopback HTTP boundary is described, not drawn as an import.

example.title: One browser-initiated lesson request
example.description: Track what the scan proves: browser player/canvas sources, Python server/store/narration/render sources, and review sources. No measured timings or generated files are claimed.

beats.title: Browser UI reaches the loopback studio
beats.question: How does a browser lesson action reach the Python visual server?
beats.insight: Player and canvas are TypeScript sources; server.py binds only 127.0.0.1 and accepts local JSON. Scan shows no browser-to-Python import; the boundary is local HTTP, not a static edge.

presentation.why: Shows where interaction code lives without inventing a runtime call across languages.
presentation.visualEvidence: Focus highlights LiveLessonPlayer and NativeLessonCanvas and their scanned NativeLessonCanvas reference; server container stays separate with its loopback bind excerpt.

continuity.bridge: Start with where a learner click lives: the browser player and native canvas, then ask where validated lessons come from.

beats.visibleOperation: Before: full file graph. Change: focus browser groups and highlight LiveLessonPlayer to NativeLessonCanvas reference. After: reader sees playback/selection live in TS and loopback server as a separate Python container.
beats.safeguard: Do not read the loopback HTTP request as an internet or cloud call; server.py allows only local studio requests.

beats.title: Server prepares validated lesson and render choice
beats.question: What does the Python visual service contribute before anything is shown?
beats.insight: server.py hosts VisualService, BrowserLessonStore validates planner JSON, NarrationStore caches clips, render_backends selects local-ce or Generative Manim. All are static references inside one Python container.

presentation.why: Groups 8 Python files into one function container so internal references do not look like runtime dataflow.
presentation.visualEvidence: Focus stays on src/assistant/visual; inspection reveals server to browser_lessons, narration, render_backends and frame_review references plus BrowserLessonStore and NarrationStore definitions.

continuity.bridge: The browser defines what to play, but where do validated lessons, cached narration and render choice come from? Inspect the Python container next.

beats.visibleOperation: Before: browser focus retained. Change: focus Python container and expand server, browser_lessons, narration and render_backends children. After: reader sees preparation and validation live in Python with no runtime values shown.
beats.safeguard: Do not treat internal references as observed execution order and do not invent databases, queues or model outputs.

beats.title: Render, frame-review and narrated playback
beats.question: How are pixels and narration checked before the learner presses play?
beats.insight: frame_review and native_review capture actual native frames for vision review; runner launches the local studio; LiveLessonPlayer and usePrototypeNarration drive resumable NarrationTransport playback. No frame bytes or audio URLs are recorded by the scan.

presentation.why: Links the two renderers, two review paths and narration transport without claiming a measured render or playback trace.
presentation.visualEvidence: Focus highlights review/render sources in Python and narration/playback sources in TypeScript; active import edges show NarrationTransport and timeline reuse, with review instruction excerpts inspectable.

continuity.bridge: Preparation explains the lesson object, but how are rendered frames checked and how does narration stay with playback? Follow the review and playback references.

beats.visibleOperation: Before: Python preparation focus. Change: focus review sources plus player and prototype narration and highlight their scanned NarrationTransport references. After: reader sees two review modules and client-side resumable playback as separate static responsibilities.
beats.safeguard: Do not claim inspected frames, verdicts, timings or audio were executed; the scan records definitions and imports only.
